correctness.rationale: For real N×N Euler matrix E_N(r) with indices 0≤k≤j<N, β=r(1−r)∈[0,1/4], Parseval gives each row-energy as mean_θ(1−a)^j with a=4β sin²(θ/2)∈[0,1]. Summing geometric powers gives S_N=mean_θ[1−(1−a)^N]/a. Replacing discrete powers with e^(−Na) gives H_N=∫_0^N e^(−2βt)I0(2βt)dt=N e^(−2Nβ)[I0(2Nβ)+I1(2Nβ)] by differentiation. Factoring e^(−Na)−(1−a)^N and using 0≤e^(−a)−(1−a)≤a²/2 yields an average error in [0,1/2), including a=0 by continuous extension; N≥2 bound uses Na e^(−(N−1)a)≤N/[e(N−1)]≤2/e, N=1 direct. For β=λ/N, x=λ(2−2cosθ)≤4L and N≥8L, the convergent logarithm expansion N log(1−x/N)=−x−x²/(2N)−δ with 0≤δ≤2x³/(3N²), plus t≤5x²/(6N), bounds pointwise remainder by (2x²/3+25x³/72)/N and hence by (32L²/3+200L³/9)/N; the leading angular correction is K(λ)=λe^(−2λ)(I0(2λ)−I1(2λ)). This proves both endpoint choices r=0,1 and N=1, reflection symmetry r↔1−r and both asserted asymptotic regimes. I independently evaluated direct binomial sums, Bessel series, exact center identities, angular moments and critical residuals; finite tests corroborate, not prove, all N.
residual_risks: No claim that uniform constant 1/2 is sharp or that individual singular values are controlled; critical O(1/N) is restricted to N≥8L.

value.rationale: The finite squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm is a natural aggregate singular-value invariant of an important classical summability family, distinct from already studied infinite-dimensional induced norms. A single explicit Bessel proxy with uniform bounded error controls all 0≤r≤1 and all N, identifying operator-energy behavior even as the smoothing scale moves with N. The critical λ/N formula supplies a nonzero order-one correction, distinguishing a genuine discrete-to-continuous effect that is not mechanically implied by a leading Gaussian or Bessel asymptotic. This is a motivated quantitative structural lemma, not a renamed textbook identity, arbitrary finite slice, or tiny unmotivated improvement.
residual_risks: The absolute error <1/2 constant is conservative; no optimality or individual singular-value information proved.
